messages:
anya: Heads-up — I ran a 2h apples-to-apples suite comparing our old kernel-selector vs the new adaptive kernel policy on long-context prefills. Seeing ~18% regression in p95 prefill latency on mixtures with 50% >8k sequences.

matt: ouch. is that on synthetic replay or production traces?

anya: Replay harness with shuffled prod traces (keeps seqlen dist). Also validated with a small synthetic mix to isolate seqlen. benchbot posted the metrics summary below.

benchbot: SUMMARY: run=apples_v2, model=gptx-large, nodes=4, policy=adaptive-kernel-v2, duration=7200s, p50_prefill=420ms (+2%), p95_prefill=1180ms (+18%), p99_prefill=2200ms (+12%), tokens/s=45k (-5%).

liam: did the profiler show where time went? prefill is mostly matmuls + kv-copy, but kernel swap could cost layout conversions.

anya: yea, perf profile looks like more time in `kv_restore` and `attn_fwd` (the fused kernel). On the old policy requests pinned to the fp16-fused kernel; the adaptive policy chose int8-approx kernel for some checkpoints because it estimates lower token cost.

matt: int8 being slower for long seqs rings a bell — kernel's tiling assumes small seqlen to benefit cache. For >8k it incurs extra passes. Can you attach the flame diff?

anya: pasted snippet from the flame (trimmed):
```
old: attn_fwd_fused                   34.2%
old: kv_restore                       12.1%
new: attn_fwd_int8                    45.7%  <-- 11.5% increase
new: kv_restore                       18.3%  <-- 6.2% increase
```

sara: so adaptive policy mispredicted cost for long prefill. We need a policy tweak: prefer fused fp16 when seqlen_estimate > 4k OR when prefill_ratio > 0.6.

liam: agree. Also, the replay harness masks warm cache behavior — prefill-heavy workloads exercise kv_restore more because we do many full sequence pushes. We should run a microbenchmark: single-request prefill of 12k tokens across kernels to measure single-call latency.

anya: ran that:
```
cmd: ./bench/replay --model gptx-large --kernel fp16-fused --seqlen 12288 --mode single
result: 980ms
cmd: ./bench/replay --model gptx-large --kernel int8-approx --seqlen 12288 --mode single
result: 1180ms
```

matt: consistent with flame. So the adaptive selection logic that optimizes for tokens/s avg is picking int8 for throughput but sacrifices tail. For prefill-dominant traffic we care about prefill latency.

anya: proposing: 1) add a context-aware heuristic to kernel-selector: if prefill_fraction_est > 0.3 OR seqlen_est > 4096 => prefer fp16-fused. 2) add unit in replay harness to run both kernels on same trace and produce per-request kernel mapping to ensure apples-to-apples mapping. 3) canary the policy on dedicated cluster with traffic split 5/95.

matt: +1. Also add a metric in console: kernel_choice label on traces so we can slice p95 by kernel. That will make postmortems easier.

infra-bot: config update proposed: `adaptive-kernel-v2+prefill-guard`. Pending review.

liam: for the harness change, keep the same RNG seed and request order for fairness. If we run kernel A then kernel B back-to-back, cache will favor second run. So better: create two parallel runs, A and B, with identical streams seeded identically and rotate host assignment.

anya: good point — I'll implement dual-run harness with deterministic seeding. Suggested command:
```
./bench/harness --trace replay.json --seed 42 --kernel-override fp16-fused --nodes 4 --run-id apples_v2_fp16
./bench/harness --trace replay.json --seed 42 --kernel-override int8-approx --nodes 4 --run-id apples_v2_int8
```

matt: and log per-request: request_id, seqlen, prefill_tokens, kernel_used, latency_ms. Keep lines CSV for ingestion.

anya: will do. Also adding a small synthetic mix generator that creates prefill-dominant sessions: 60% sessions with prefill >= 8k, 30% 1-2k, 10% chat. That will expose policy sensitivity.

sara: schedule the canary after we have kernel-slice dashboards. We should measure both throughput and token-economics (tokens/s and cost per token). If fp16 increases GPU time but reduces tails, it might be better overall for SLOs.

anya: timeline: I'll push harness + kernel-slice metrics today, run dual-runs overnight, and open a PR for the policy change. Can folks review the PR tomorrow?

matt: can review midday. also add a note for post-run: diff p95 on prefill-only subset, and add flamegraphs for top 3 offending kernels.

benchbot: FYI: I kicked off the dual-run job with seed=42. job ids: apples_v2_fp16: 4821, apples_v2_int8: 4822. I'll post when done. :rocket:

anya: thanks. if we confirm the regression is policy-driven we can roll back adaptive-kernel-v2 or gate it behind prefill-guard until we have a smarter cost model.

liam: also file a perf ticket (ENG-PRF-###) so we track root cause and decision.

anya: filed ENG-PRF-348. linking results when benchbot finishes.

matt: thanks all. short action items: anya: harness + metrics, liam: microbenchmark triage, sara: dashboard + canary plan.

anya: done. ping me in thread if anything else.
